gen-dafont-klill-fs-alpino: Klill draws every diagonal as stout as its uprights, with no hairlines anywhere. Alpino follows in a tall, cozy sans-serif whose short-looking ascenders and tight spacing make paragraphs feel snug and casual rather than stiff.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab arrives grounded, a text serif with tall lowercase bodies. Klill sits above it in sturdy sans-serif strokes with no hairlines at all, so the headline feels blunt and the copy beneath it feels refined.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-paquito: Wire-thin strokes give Klill its look, with no swell from line to line. Paquito's serif below has a minimal drop from lowercase to caps, so the two feel confident, approachable and pleasantly unlike in texture.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-supreme: Klill has r, n and m whose arches match their stems, which makes it feel tidy and sturdy. And Supreme's heavy-looking band of text, with letters held open, gives the sans a crisp counterpart in the same spirit.
gen-dafont-klill-fs-trench-slab: Klill has a pipe-cleaner look to its strokes, with curve endings kept well apart and big-bodied lowercase letters. Trench Slab adds dignity.
gen-dafont-klill-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, with open mouths on its curves, a small step up to the capitals and a pen line holding one width. Klill shares that build.
gen-dafont-klill-satoshi: Tall, open, and unfussy. Klill brings big-bodied lowercase and one-width strokes, and Satoshi picks up that thread with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e that never looks squeezed shut.
gen-dafont-klill-work-sans: Klill sets the tone with big-bodied lowercase and curve endings kept well apart, all in one stroke thickness. Work Sans carries that on below, its c tips never creeping together and its high mean line keeping long paragraphs feeling modern and unhurried.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-bespoke-serif: Loose, wide, and friendly, like lettering from a rolling-ball pen. Bespoke Serif settles into a long read with an authoritative serif voice, its thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-sentient: Sentient reads as pinched and closed-in, with crossbars a touch thinner than the stems. But Lemon Milk's rounded, open letters, drawn with a nib that never swells, loosen the whole pairing up.
